levels.title: Servicing

lessons.title: How an Android phone starts
lessons.summary: Follow the chain from BootROM to the home screen, and learn why each link matters before you flash.

quiz.prompt: What is the first code that runs when an Android phone powers on?
quiz.explanation: BootROM is burned into the chipset. It loads and verifies the next stage, usually the bootloader.

quiz.prompt: What does the boot partition contain on most modern Android phones?
options: The kernel and a small ramdisk
quiz.explanation: The boot image holds the kernel plus a ramdisk. On A/B devices it is paired with an inactive slot copy.

quiz.prompt: Why does a failed system flash on an A/B phone often still boot?
options: Because the battery hides the failure
Because the other slot can still boot
Because Android always has two batteries
quiz.explanation: A/B devices keep two bootable slots. The bootloader can fall back to the slot that was not being written.

lessons.title: USB modes, drivers, and authorisation
lessons.summary: Tell MTP, ADB, Fastboot, and download modes apart, and fix the Windows side before blaming the phone.

quiz.prompt: The phone shows up in Windows but adb devices lists it as unauthorized. What is the correct next step?
options: Unlock the phone and accept the USB debugging prompt
quiz.explanation: Authorisation happens on the phone. Unlock it, then approve the RSA fingerprint prompt.

quiz.prompt: Which mode is used for fastboot flash commands?
quiz.explanation: Fastboot talks to the bootloader, not to a running Android system.

quiz.prompt: Why should you avoid random USB driver packs from unofficial sites?
options: They can be outdated, bundled with unwanted software, or unsafe
quiz.explanation: Use the vendor's official driver page or the Google USB Driver. Unofficial bundles are a supply-chain risk.

lessons.title: Reading device facts without changing anything
lessons.summary: Collect the model, build, patch level, and bootloader state first. Good notes prevent wrong firmware.

quiz.prompt: Which property identifies the exact installed build?
quiz.explanation: ro.build.display.id is the build string. The model alone is not enough to choose firmware.

quiz.prompt: What does ro.boot.flash.locked=1 usually mean?
quiz.explanation: A value of 1 means the bootloader reports a locked state. 0 usually means unlocked.

quiz.prompt: Why record the security patch date before servicing?
options: It helps match compatible firmware and detect downgrade problems
It is required to charge the phone
quiz.explanation: Patch level and build number are key inputs when choosing firmware and predicting anti-rollback behaviour.

lessons.title: Bootloader unlocking, legally and safely
lessons.summary: Understand what unlocking changes, which phones allow it, and why it always starts with a backup.

quiz.prompt: What is a normal side effect of unlocking the bootloader on most phones?
quiz.explanation: Unlocking usually forces a factory reset to protect user data. Back up first.

quiz.prompt: Which phones can be unlocked with fastboot flashing unlock?
options: Only phones whose vendor allows it and exposes the command
Only phones with a broken screen
quiz.explanation: Vendors control unlock policy. Many carrier or regional models block it entirely.

quiz.prompt: What should you check before promising a customer an unlock?
options: Vendor policy, carrier lock, warranty terms, and their explicit consent
quiz.explanation: Unlocking can void warranty and trip security features. Owner consent and vendor policy come first.

lessons.title: Choosing and flashing factory firmware
lessons.summary: Match the exact model and region, verify the archive, and flash in the order the vendor documents.

quiz.prompt: What is the safest source for factory firmware?
options: The phone vendor's official support or firmware page
An unofficial mirror with no checksums
quiz.explanation: Only the vendor's official channel can be trusted for signed, current firmware.

quiz.prompt: Why must you not mix firmware from a different model variant?
options: Partitions and radio firmware may not match the hardware and can brick the phone
It only affects the camera app
quiz.explanation: Variants can differ in modem, partition layout, and signing keys. A mismatch can make the device unbootable.

quiz.prompt: What should you do immediately after flashing and before handing the phone back?
options: Boot it, test radio/IMEI, charging, sensors, and confirm the build number
quiz.explanation: A flash is not finished until the device boots and the critical hardware paths are verified.

lessons.title: Custom recovery and sideload boundaries
lessons.summary: Know the difference between recovery, fastbootd, and a running system before you wipe or sideload.

quiz.prompt: What does adb sideload require?
options: A booted Android system with USB debugging only
A recovery or update mode that accepts sideload
quiz.explanation: Sideload runs through recovery or an update mode. Plain Android does not accept an OTA package this way.

quiz.prompt: What is fastbootd?
options: A userspace fastboot implementation inside newer recovery images
quiz.explanation: Fastbootd runs in userspace and can handle logical partitions that classic bootloader fastboot cannot.

quiz.prompt: What is the main risk of a custom recovery on an encrypted device?
options: It cannot read encrypted data without the right keys or format
quiz.explanation: Encryption and metadata encryption can block access. Formatting data destroys it, so confirm what the owner needs first.

lessons.title: Root models: Magisk, KernelSU, and APatch
lessons.summary: Compare how modern root solutions patch boot images, and what that means for updates and integrity checks.

quiz.prompt: What does Magisk patch to gain root?
options: The boot image (or init_boot on some devices)
quiz.explanation: Magisk patches the ramdisk inside the boot image, or init_boot where the ramdisk lives there.

quiz.prompt: Why does a system update often remove root?
options: Updates replace the boot partition or slot
quiz.explanation: OTA updates write a fresh boot image. Root must be reapplied to the new image after the update.

quiz.prompt: What should you warn the owner about after rooting?
options: Banking and DRM apps may refuse to run, and security guarantees change
quiz.explanation: Root weakens the verified boot model. Some apps detect it, and the owner must accept the trade-off.

lessons.title: Brick triage: soft brick, hard brick, and when to stop
lessons.summary: Separate a bootloop from a dead bootloader, and avoid making a recoverable phone worse.

quiz.prompt: Which symptom most often indicates a soft brick?
options: No vibration, no screen, and no USB enumeration at all
A bootloop or recovery loop with the bootloader still reachable
The phone charges normally and boots fine
quiz.explanation: If the bootloader or recovery still responds, the device is usually recoverable with the right firmware.

quiz.prompt: What is the safest first action for a phone stuck in a bootloop after a bad flash?
options: Flash random firmware from the first search result
Stop, identify the exact model and build, and read the vendor recovery procedure
Open the phone and remove the battery
quiz.explanation: Accurate identification and the vendor's documented recovery path prevent a soft brick from becoming permanent.

quiz.prompt: When should you stop and refer the device to an authorised service centre?
options: When the bootloader is locked and no official recovery path exists
When the phone has a case on
When the owner speaks another language
quiz.explanation: Without an official path or an unlocked bootloader, forcing EDL or test-point modes can destroy the device.

lessons.title: Post-service quality checks
lessons.summary: Turn a successful flash into a trustworthy repair with a repeatable end-of-job checklist.

quiz.prompt: Which check belongs in every post-flash test?
options: Calls/SMS data, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cameras, sensors, charging, and the build number
quiz.explanation: A repair is complete only when the main hardware paths and the installed build are verified.

quiz.prompt: What should be recorded before returning the phone?
options: Model, serial, old and new build, actions performed, and test results
A list of the owner's contacts
quiz.explanation: A service record protects both the owner and the technician and makes later troubleshooting possible.

quiz.prompt: The phone boots but the SIM is not detected after a flash. What is the best next step?
options: Check the modem firmware/region match and inspect the SIM tray, then reflash the correct package
Flash a random modem from another model
quiz.explanation: Missing radio usually points to a firmware/variant mismatch or hardware. Verify the correct package before reflashing.
